thread:
maria-ledesma: Heads up — we just saw a cluster-wide spike of PCIe AER/Xid messages and NVLink link flaps centered on rack-12. Impact: inference p50 latency +30% for 10:02–10:07 UTC, a few OOM-ish task restarts.

ajay-chen: I pulled telemetry: pattern is bursts of AER 'uncorrectable' on gpu-node-12a GPU[0-3], followed by kernel pci_bus resets. Attaching dmesg snippet below.

maria-ledesma: ```
[ 10.03.512] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Severity=Uncorrected)
[ 10.03.512] gpu0: nvlink: link 1 down
[ 10.03.517] GPU: Xid 43: RmInitVBlank timed out
[ 10.04.001] pci 0000:65:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Uncorrected, type=Physical Layer
```

ops-bot: alert summary: rack-12 reported 4 degraded nodes, 12 hosts scanned, 3 hosts crossed error threshold. Auto-scaling paused on affected pools.

leo-garcia: Quick hypothesis — these look like transient AERs triggered by sudden KV-cache hot bursts (long seq lengths) causing NVLink retransmits and then PCIe retrain. Could be riser contact or a firmware cornercase in the platform.

ajay-chen: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) cordon+drain the 3 most-errant nodes (gpu-node-12a/b/c). 2) throttle high-token jobs via the scheduler (limit burst concurrency). 3) collect lspci -vvv, edac and driver logs for affected hosts. Commands: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12a
kubectl drain gpu-node-12a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
ssh gpu-node-12a 'dmesg | grep -i -E "AER|nvlink|Xid" > /tmp/aer-gpu-node-12a.log'
```

maria-ledesma: did a quick memory/ECC check — ECC corrected counts are rising on GPU0 and GPU1. Ran: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER` — pushing logs to /var/logs/gpu/1887654321/.

ops-bot: note: we temporarily disabled burst autoscaling for the affected autoscaling group to avoid mass scheduling into degraded nodes.

sre-oncall: Proposed triage plan: 
1) Immediate (0–2h): cordon+drain the 3 hosts, route traffic to spare capacity (fall back pool in region eu-west-1). Keep one host un-drained for trace capture.
2) Near-term (2–24h): run PCIe stress & NVLink stress test, lspci -vvv, vendor PCIe diagnostic (packed logs uploaded to S3 path: s3://redwood-debug/rack-12/1887654321).
3) Replacement (1–7 days): if errors persist after reseating riser/BIOS microcode toggle, schedule riser/card RMA for the flagged host.
4) Postmortem: capture token/seq distribution and correlate to workload types to tune batching.

Cost note: draining 3 hosts reduces cluster GPU capacity by ~18% during mitigation window; forecasting ~3–6% observable QPS loss to frontends unless we scale fallback pool. Ops: expect ~2–4k USD incremental infra cost for cross-region failover if used >4h.

ajay-chen: I'm collecting kernel trace: perf record + trace-cmd and will open vendor SR with logs. Also going to try disabling PCIe ASPM on one dev host to see if retrain frequency drops (`pcie_aspm=off`). Will report results.

maria-ledesma: status update — cordoned/drained gpu-node-12a/b/c, one node held for trace. nvlink flaps stopped on drained hosts, errors still intermittently on gpu-node-12d. Flagged gpu-node-12d for deeper inspection.

sre-oncall: action items assigned: 
- ajay-chen: collect vendor trace & open SR (ETA 3h)
- leo-garcia: hardware inspect gpu-node-12d riser + reseat (ETA 6h)
- maria-ledesma: followup perf traces + postmortem notes (ETA EOD)

maria-ledesma: if nothing else, marking this thread 'monitoring' — I'll post updates. If errors recur after reseat, we'll schedule RMA for the affected card. :wave:
